title: Italians seek answers in death of expatriate; Man died after being in Quebec police custody
article: Quebec's Italian community is calling for a public inquiry into the death of a 32-year-old emigrant from that country who died here last week after being transferred to a detention centre by police.
The case has also caught the attention of the Italian government.
Claudio Castagnetta was arrested on Sept. 18 outside a convenience store for public disorder. He was walking barefoot in the store and refused to leave the premises.
The owner, Daniel Racine, called the police because he was bothering clients. He said Castagnetta's behaviour was bizarre, but he showed no signs of violence.
There are media reports that Castagnetta was bipolar, but he was not taking medication and his family says he didn't have psychological problems.
Quebec City police said Castagnetta resisted arrest by stiffening his body. It took six officers to handcuff him and they also had to use a stun gun.

Castagnetta - who had no criminal record - was taken into custody overnight and appeared in court the next day to face charges of obstructing justice. He was returned to the detention centre but was then taken to a local hospital. He had head injuries and he never recovered. It is unclear how and when Castagnetta suffered those injuries.
The provincial police are investigating the incident and refused comment.
But according to Castagnetta's family - who flew in from Palermo, Sicilia, after his death - he harmed himself in the prison van while he was being transferred to the detention centre.

"What happened exactly? We don't know," said Ricardo Rossini, Italy's honorary consul in Quebec City. He has been with the Castagnetta family since they arrived here on Sunday. "They have a lot of questions and they want to understand what really went on. It's incomprehensible for them because Claudio was not violent. He was a very nice guy and everybody liked him."
